title: Inspection Request Form (M&E)
source: spec/reference/inspection-request-form.html — the same sheet the print-step RFI cover page replicates (SPEC §12, handover 2026-08-05 task 2). This template does NOT replace that cover. The cover stays what it is: a page-1 decoration on ONE record, whose contractor sign-off is copied from that record's own signature and whose inspector block prints blank for handwriting. This template is the sheet as a RECORD in its own right — its own serial, its own two signatures, its own status workflow — for the two cases the cover cannot serve: (1) one request covering SEVERAL test records, and (2) an inspector / engineer who is not the person who signed the test form, and who signs the request itself (on device, or through a remote sign-off link).

sections.title: Scope / Remarks
sections._note:
`page_break_before` on the opening section is the grouping idiom, not a layout instruction: `paginate` gives every section a sheet of its own unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op because it is already page 1 (same as `pa-system-test.json`, `fire-alarm-test.json`).

**THE REQUEST IS ONE A4 PAGE ON THE PAPER AND THREE HERE. Measured, not estimated** (Chrome, 2026-08-18, against a filled record: five covered records, prose in Scope / Remarks and in the result comment). The print body budget is **881px**; the whole request came to **1425px** as one page, 62% over. The cost is the two sign-off grids at 339px each — a third of a sheet apiece — which is why a form the paper fits in one page cannot be fitted in fewer than three here. This is the codebase norm, not a defect: the app's sheets are far less dense than the source HTMLs, and a one-A4 paper form usually becomes two app pages.

A two-page split was tried first (break before `contractor_sign_off` only) and REJECTED on measurement: page 2 came to 892.8px against the 881px budget — 11.8px over — and page 1 had 19.3px spare, so a sixth covered record would have overflowed it too. Do not go back to it.

The split now is: **page 1** request details + scope + covered records, **page 2** declaration + contractor sign-off, **page 3** inspection result + inspector sign-off. Filled headroom is 183 / 353 / 368px. Page 1 deliberately gets the smallest share of content because it carries the only block that GROWS — `attached_records` — and 183px is about five more rows, so roughly **ten covered records before the page spills**. `paginate` splits on sections, never inside a table, so an eleventh row overflows the sheet rather than starting a page 2; if a request ever needs more, give `attached_records` its own page rather than widening the others.

There is still no top-level `footer` — a `footer` block always prints on a page of its own (`PrintView` adds one), which would make it four.

The paper's Scope / Remarks is a ruled box the engineer writes into, and that is all this is.

**Header decisions** (recorded here because `headerFieldSchema` is strict and carries no `_note`):

- **IRF No.** is the site-assigned request number, which the paper leaves for the engineer to write and the print-step cover therefore prints blank. Here it is a filled, required field — a request the consultant cannot cite by number is not a request. It is NOT this record's `serial_no`: the serial is the app's own sequence and already prints in the page footer (SPEC §7). Two numbers on purpose, because they belong to two different registers.
- **Discipline** is a `dropdown`, not five booleans: the paper prints five checkboxes on one row and exactly one is ticked. It is asked of the record rather than fixed by the template — a request bundling an ACMV duct test with the electrical supply feeding it is filed under whichever discipline the consultant inspects it as. Same decision as the print-step cover, whose discipline is user-chosen and not auto-bound to the template (SPEC §12).
- **Other (specify)** is the free-text box beside the paper's `Other:` tick. Nothing enforces that it is filled only when Discipline is `Other` — the schema has no cross-field conditional and one box does not justify inventing one.
- **Drawing No.** defaults to the wording the site team writes on nearly every issued request, which is what the cover already seeds (`RFI_DRAWING_NO_DEFAULT`). A request against a single drawing overtypes it.

sections.title: Test Records Covered by This Request
sections._note:
THE ONE BLOCK THAT IS NOT ON THE PAPER. Everything else in this template is the source sheet; this table is an addition, and it is the reason the template exists — it is what lets ONE request cover SEVERAL test records, which the print-step cover cannot do (it is bolted to a single record). On the paper the same job is done by writing the attached forms into the Scope / Remarks box as prose.

It is deliberately a plain typed list, not a live link to other records. Rows carry the record's printed title and its serial (`Record No.` — the serial the app assigns at draft → completed, which is exactly the number printed in that record's page footer), so the consultant can match each line to a sheet in the bundle by eye. Making it a foreign key into the register would tie a signed request to records that can still change status underneath it, and nothing in the schema expresses a cross-record reference — a template is data (Hard Rule #4).

`min_rows` is 1, so a request covering one test form prints one line rather than a block of empty ruling. About **ten rows fit** before page 1 spills — measured, see the `scope` note.

Column widths are set from a measured record, not guessed: `record_no` is 22% because at 18% a serial of the app's own format (`AMK3-DAL-0031`) wrapped onto two lines, which on a table whose whole purpose is citing record numbers is the one thing it must not do. The 4% came out of `test_record` and `equipment`, both of which carry prose that wraps anyway.

If the consultant on a job rejects the departure from their accepted paper form, DELETE THIS SECTION and list the records in Scope / Remarks instead: nothing else in the template depends on it, and the remaining sections are the source sheet block for block.

sections.title: Declaration

rows.description: We, the Main Contractor / Contractor / Nominated Sub-Contractor / Sub-Contractor have already carried out Preliminary Inspections of the works to ensure that they are in accordance with the Specification, Scope of Works, and Contract documentation requirements and that the works are complete and ready for Inspection.

sections._note:
Verbatim from the source form, and character-for-character the same sentence as `RFI_DECLARATION` in `lib/rfi-cover.ts` — the parity test pins the two together so a reword reaches both or neither.

The paper prints the paragraph as prose above the contractor's signature; here it carries a checkbox. The signature below it is the binding act either way, so the tick adds nothing legally — it is there because a row in a standard section is what a fixed sentence renders as in this library, and a tick the contractor makes before signing is closer to the paper's intent than a sentence with no control at all. It is not `required`: the signature is what gates the workflow.

sections.title: Contractor Sign-off

signatures._note: The paper labels this block and the inspector's block alike — both read `Inspected By:` — and the role is carried verbatim rather than disambiguated, because the section titles above them already say which is which on screen and in print.

sections._note:
A `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer` for two reasons: the paper puts this block in the MIDDLE of the page, above the result, and a `footer` always prints on a page of its own (`PrintView` adds one), which would make a one-page form two.

`stage: "contractor"` gates draft → completed, so a request cannot be issued until the contractor has signed the declaration above it.

sections.title: Inspection Result
sections._note:
The paper's three tick boxes — PASS, FAIL, CONDITIONAL PASS — and its Comments box beneath them. Three mutually exclusive states is a `status` row; the emoji the source HTML decorates them with are screen dressing and are not carried.

**Conditional Pass maps to `outcome: "fail"`, deliberately.** A conditional pass is a pass with work still owed, and `fail` is what puts it on the outstanding-items list (SPEC §6) so it is chased rather than filed. `na`/`neutral` would drop it silently — the same call the IDF Handover form's "In Progress" state makes.

This block is filled by the INSPECTOR, not the contractor. It sits after the contractor's signature on the paper for exactly that reason, and it is why this template is worth having at all: on the print-step cover the result prints as an empty box for handwriting, because that cover has no second signer.

sections.title: Inspector / Engineer Sign-off

signatures._note: No `company_default`: the inspector is the consultant or the client's engineer, not Kenyon, so the company is theirs to enter — which is the whole point of the slot.

sections._note:
`stage: "client"` is the accepting signature (`accept`: witnessed → accepted), so the request is only closed out once the inspector has signed it.

No `witness` slot is declared, and a stage with no slots is satisfied vacuously (`satisfiedStages`), so the run is: complete (contractor signed) → submit for witness → witness → accept (inspector signed). The two intermediate steps are QA/QC moves with nothing to sign.

Because this is an ordinary signature slot on an ordinary record, the inspector can sign it through a remote sign-off link without an account (SPEC §12, `request-signature.tsx`) — which is what makes a different signer here from the one on the test form a normal case rather than a workaround.
